## Learning objectives

By the end of this demonstration, you should be able to explain what the
project's R lockfile records, how a Docker image becomes your MyBinder
session, and why we keep a record of the environment used to run an analysis.

The instructor runs the commands. You can follow along in the MyBinder session
you opened during [preparation](00_preparation.qmd); nothing needs to be
installed.

## Why this matters

Allow about two minutes. The same script can behave differently when package
versions or system libraries change. We need to describe the environment
alongside the code and the data version.

| Layer | What we record | Tool or file |
| --- | --- | --- |
| R runtime | R version | `renv.lock`, runtime information, container base image |
| R packages | Package versions and sources | renv and `renv.lock` |
| Wider environment | Operating-system libraries and rendering tools | Dockerfile and image |
| Code and configuration | The revision used for the run | Git commit |
| Actual session | Versions loaded when the analysis ran | `sessionInfo()` |

renv restores the R packages described by a lockfile. A Docker image can also
include the R interpreter, operating-system libraries, and rendering tools.
Binder starts a container from such an image in a browser. Reproducing a
result still requires the analysis code, the input data, and a successful
rerun.

## Inspect the R environment

Allow about three minutes. In the **R Console**, with the project open:

```{r health-environments-session, include = TRUE, echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE, cache = FALSE, output = TRUE, eval = TRUE}
R.version.string
.libPaths()
packageVersion("renv")
```

Compare the running version with the reference version, **4.4.1**. A lockfile
records a version; it does not switch your running R session.

```{r health-environments-lockfile, include = TRUE, echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE, cache = FALSE, output = TRUE, eval = TRUE}
lock <- renv::lockfile_read("renv.lock")
lock$R$Version
workshop_packages <- c(
  "dataspice", "meta", "pins", "quarto", "rfair", "rmarkdown",
  "synthpop", "targets", "vetiver"
)
vapply(
  workshop_packages,
  function(package) {
    record <- lock$Packages[[package]]
    if (is.null(record)) NA_character_ else record$Version
  },
  character(1)
)
renv::status()
```

The lockfile records exact package versions for the workshop. A package that
is not recorded appears as `NA`; Quarto, for example, is a command-line tool
in the image rather than an R package in the lockfile. `renv::status()` checks
whether the active library matches the lockfile.

The usual collaboration cycle is:

1. A maintainer prepares and tests the required packages.
2. The maintainer uses `renv::snapshot()` and reviews the resulting lockfile.
3. Collaborators use `renv::restore()` to obtain the recorded packages.
4. The analysis is tested in the restored environment.

The workshop's Binder image was built by restoring this lockfile, so you do not
need to run `renv::restore()` during the session.

## From a Dockerfile to RStudio on MyBinder {#environments-docker}

Allow about four minutes.

### Read the Dockerfile

A **Dockerfile** is a set of instructions for building a Docker image. Find
these instructions in the workshop's [Binder image Dockerfile](https://github.com/JBris/open-and-reproducible-science-in-r/blob/main/dockerfiles/binder/Dockerfile.1.0.0).

| Instruction | What it does in this project |
| --- | --- |
| `FROM rocker/binder:4.4.1 AS base` | Starts from Rocker’s Binder image for R 4.4.1. |
| `RUN` | Executes build steps such as installing system libraries and restoring R packages from `renv.lock`. |
| `COPY` | Adds files such as the lockfile and workshop lessons to the image. |

A **Docker build** uses these instructions and the repository files to produce
an **image**. A **container** is a running instance of an image. Each
participant runs the workshop in their own container started from the same
image.

### Follow the GitHub Actions build pipelines

The repository has two workflows that run when a GitHub release is published
or when a maintainer starts them manually. [Build Binder](https://github.com/JBris/open-and-reproducible-science-in-r/actions/workflows/build-binder.yaml)
builds the image MyBinder uses. [Build RStudio](https://github.com/JBris/open-and-reproducible-science-in-r/actions/workflows/build-rstudio.yaml)
builds a separate image for people running RStudio with Docker locally.

Each workflow checks out the source, reads `VERSION` into `APP_VERSION`, and
records a UTC build date. Docker Compose uses `APP_VERSION` to select the
Dockerfile and tag the image. The Binder job includes these two steps.

```bash
docker compose build binder
docker compose push binder
```

The first command builds the image. The second publishes the image with its
version tag to GitHub Container Registry (`ghcr.io`). The image version comes
from `VERSION` and can differ from the GitHub release tag.

### Launch the published environment

MyBinder reads the small [Binder entry point](https://github.com/JBris/open-and-reproducible-science-in-r/blob/main/binder/Dockerfile),
which selects the published Binder image with `FROM`. MyBinder prepares the
launch image and starts a container on its servers. The launch link’s
`urlpath=rstudio` setting opens the RStudio interface in your browser.

Because everyone starts from the same image, everyone has the same R version,
packages, and tools for the hands-on activities.

## Record the session

Allow about one minute. Load the data by its explicit path into a
separate environment, then save a record of the current R session.

```{r health-environments-reload, include = TRUE, echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE, cache = FALSE, output = TRUE, eval = TRUE}
raw_file <- file.path("data", "raw", "healthwellbeing.rda")
stopifnot(
  file.exists(raw_file),
  identical(
    unname(tools::md5sum(raw_file)),
    "0d74964b0b7168379a2b015cb648b326"
  )
)
data_env <- new.env(parent = baseenv())
loaded_names <- load(raw_file, envir = data_env)
stopifnot(identical(loaded_names, "HealthWellbeing"))
health <- data_env[["HealthWellbeing"]]
stopifnot(nrow(health) == 29L, ncol(health) == 5L)

source("pipelines/workshop_support.R")
output_dir <- workshop_output_dir()
dir.create(output_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
writeLines(
  capture.output(sessionInfo()),
  file.path(output_dir, "session-info.txt")
)
```

`outputs/health-wellbeing/session-info.txt` lists the loaded package versions and platform.
Later, the pipeline records the R and *meta* versions with its result. For a
MyBinder run, the image tag in `binder/Dockerfile` and the project revision
from `git rev-parse HEAD` complete the record.

## Checkpoint {#environments-checkpoint}

- You can explain which parts of the environment renv and Docker capture.
- You can trace how GitHub Actions builds and publishes the Binder image and
  how MyBinder uses it to start RStudio.
- You can distinguish the lockfile's recorded R version from the running version.
- You know where to find the session record and the package versions.

**Takeaway:** a documented environment supports reproducibility, and a
successful rerun supplies evidence. Next, we document the dataset itself.
[FAIR data documentation and assessment](03_data_documentation.qmd)

## After the workshop: record your own environment

In a new R project, use `renv::init()` to create the project library.
After installing and checking the packages your analysis uses, run
`renv::snapshot()` and review the lockfile. A collaborator can then run
`renv::restore()` with the corresponding R version.

For a container, start with an R base image such as
`FROM rocker/r-ver:4.4.1`. Add your system dependencies and restore the
package library from `renv.lock` during the build. The
[workshop's Docker setup](https://github.com/JBris/open-and-reproducible-science-in-r#usage-with-docker)
shows how this fits into a complete project.
